why: Introduces Target-Stance Extraction, a stance-detection reformulation task for social media text where the target is not given in advance; a text classification task with no bearing on agent trajectory verification.

title: A Close Look into the Calibration of Pre-trained Language Models
why: An empirical/measurement study that controls six training factors (data difficulty, sample count, steps, tunable parameters, scale, pretraining) to test whether the assumed-sufficient claim 'PLMs become calibrated during training' actually holds, finding it does not -- structurally a good exemplar of the A2 archetype (stress-testing an assumed-sufficient paradigm with controlled factors), though the domain (confidence calibration) is unrelated to milestone verification.

title: An AMR-based Link Prediction Approach for Document-level Event Argument Extraction
why: TARA reformulates document-level event argument extraction as link prediction over a tailored AMR graph; an information-extraction architecture paper with no connection to verifier locality or checkpoint bypass.

title: A Synthetic Data Generation Framework for Grounded Dialogues
why: Proposes a framework for synthesizing grounded dialogue training data to augment knowledge-grounded response generation, unrelated to agent-task verification.

title: Automated Metrics for Medical Multi-Document Summarization Disagree with Human Evaluations
why: Shows that automated summarization metrics disagree with human judgments on medical multi-document summarization quality; a metric-validity study for text summarization, not for milestone/state verifiers in agent tasks.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Model Capabilities for Conditional Generation
why: Benchmarks LLM conditional-generation capability across many NLG tasks with few-shot and finetuning setups; a general NLG capability benchmark, not about checkpoint/verifier-locality bypass in agent trajectories.

title: BITE: Textual Backdoor Attacks with Iterative Trigger Injection
why: BITE is a textual backdoor-attack method that iteratively injects trigger words into training data for text classifiers; an adversarial-poisoning paper unrelated to verification-of-milestones.

title: Are Message Passing Neural Networks Really Helpful for Knowledge Graph Completion?
why: Empirically questions whether message-passing GNNs are needed for knowledge-graph completion versus simpler MLPs; a KG-embedding architecture study with no relation to agent checkpoint verification.

title: Binary and Ternary Natural Language Generation
why: Studies binary/ternary weight-and-activation quantization of generative transformers (BART/mBART) for summarization and translation efficiency; a model-compression paper unrelated to verifier locality.

title: A Universal Discriminator for Zero-Shot Generalization
why: Proposes a single discriminator model D(x) for zero-shot generalization across NLP tasks by scoring candidate completions; a discriminative-modeling paper with no connection to prerequisite-state or checkpoint verification.

title: Attributable and Scalable Opinion Summarization
why: HERCULES is an unsupervised hierarchical discrete-latent-space method for attributable, scalable opinion summarization from customer reviews; unrelated to agent-task milestone verification.

title: Backdooring Neural Code Search
why: Demonstrates a backdoor attack against neural code-search models via poisoned training data; a security/adversarial-ML paper on retrieval models, not on agent checkpoint verification.

title: Answering Ambiguous Questions via Iterative Prompting
why: AmbigPrompt iteratively prompts a QA model to compose multiple answers to ambiguous open-domain questions; an open-domain QA method with no bearing on milestone-verifier locality.

title: A Survey on Zero Pronoun Translation
why: A survey of zero-pronoun translation methods and datasets in machine translation; a translation-linguistics survey unrelated to agent verification.

title: A Gradient Control Method for Backdoor Attacks on Parameter-Efficient Tuning
why: Proposes a gradient-control method to prevent 'backdoor forgetting' during parameter-efficient fine-tuning after a backdoor has been injected; a security paper on PEFT, unrelated to checkpoint bypass in agent verification.

title: Automatic Annotation of Direct Speech in Written French Narratives
why: Presents a framework for automatically tagging direct-speech spans in written French narratives; a sequence-labeling task for literary text, unrelated to agent milestone verification.

title: A Survey for Efficient Open Domain Question Answering
why: Surveys efficiency techniques (retriever-reader, retriever-only, generator-only) for open-domain QA systems; a systems-efficiency survey with no bearing on verifier locality or checkpoint bypass.

title: Abductive Commonsense Reasoning Exploiting Mutually Exclusive Explanations
why: LiPoR trains models to distinguish plausible from implausible abductive-reasoning explanations via posterior regularization without plausibility annotations; a commonsense-reasoning training method unrelated to agent-task verification.

title: A Survey on Asking Clarification Questions Datasets in Conversational Systems
why: A survey comparing datasets for training conversational systems to ask clarification questions; unrelated to prerequisite-state or checkpoint verification.

title: Beyond Contrastive Learning: A Variational Generative Model for Multilingual Retrieval
why: Proposes a variational generative model for multilingual sentence-embedding retrieval as an alternative to contrastive learning; a representation-learning paper unrelated to milestone verification.

title: An Invariant Learning Characterization of Controlled Text Generation
why: Characterizes controlled text generation as learning an attribute classifier that must generalize (be invariant) across different prompt-induced text distributions; an invariant-learning framing of attribute control, not of verifier-locality-versus-global-truth in multi-step tasks.

title: Are Human Explanations Always Helpful? Towards Objective Evaluation of Human Natural Language Explanations
why: Evaluates whether human-written free-text explanations actually help downstream model prediction, introducing an explanation-helpfulness metric; unrelated to checkpoint/milestone verification.

title: ALERT: Adapt Language Models to Reasoning Tasks
why: ALERT is a benchmark testing whether LLMs apply genuine reasoning skills versus memorized training-corpus patterns across logic/arithmetic/spatial tasks; a reasoning-generalization benchmark, not a study of milestone-verifier bypass or a terminal-state oracle.

title: Aggregating Multiple Heuristic Signals as Supervision for Unsupervised Automated Essay Scoring
why: ULRA trains an unsupervised automated essay-scoring model by aggregating multiple noisy heuristic quality signals via pairwise rank aggregation; an essay-scoring method unrelated to agent-task verification.

title: APOLLO: A Simple Approach for Adaptive Pretraining of Language Models for Logical Reasoning
why: APOLLO proposes a selective-masking adaptive-pretraining objective to improve logical reasoning in language models; a pretraining-objective paper unrelated to checkpoint verification.

title: A Crosslingual Investigation of Conceptualization in 1335 Languages
why: Investigates cross-linguistic differences in how 1,335 languages conceptualize/lexicalize meaning via aligned concept embeddings; a typological semantics study unrelated to agent verification.

title: BERM: Training the Balanced and Extractable Representation for Matching to Improve Generalization Ability of Dense Retrieval
why: BERM trains a balanced, extractable dense-retrieval representation to improve out-of-domain generalization of retrieval matching; a representation-learning paper for retrieval, unrelated to milestone verification.

title: ArgAnalysis35K : A large-scale dataset for Argument Quality Analysis
why: Introduces ArgAnalysis35K, a large dataset of argument-analysis pairs from parliamentary debating with a relevance-scoring model; an argument-quality dataset paper unrelated to checkpoint bypass.

title: KNOW How to Make Up Your Mind! Adversarially Detecting and Alleviating Inconsistencies in Natural Language Explanations
why: eKnowIA is an adversarial attack that finds pairs of individually-plausible natural-language explanations from the same model that are mutually contradictory, plus a knowledge-grounding fix; while it shares a 'locally plausible parts, globally inconsistent whole' flavor, it targets explanation faithfulness/consistency of a single model's rationales rather than independent milestone-scoped state verifiers versus a disjoint terminal-state oracle, so the connection is too indirect to count as a real method-twin.

title: Bidirectional Generative Framework for Cross-domain Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis
why: Proposes a bidirectional text-to-label/label-to-text generative framework for cross-domain aspect-based sentiment analysis; a sentiment-analysis domain-adaptation paper unrelated to agent verification.

title: A Novel Table-to-Graph Generation Approach for Document-Level Joint Entity and Relation Extraction
why: Proposes a table-to-graph generation approach for joint document-level entity and relation extraction; an information-extraction architecture paper unrelated to checkpoint/milestone verification.

title: AMR-based Network for Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis
why: APARN is an AMR-based network for aspect-based sentiment analysis; a sentiment-analysis architecture paper unrelated to verifier locality or prerequisite-state bypass.

title: Automatic Creation of Named Entity Recognition Datasets by Querying Phrase Representations
why: HighGEN automatically builds high-coverage pseudo-dictionaries for weakly-supervised NER dataset creation via phrase-representation retrieval; an NER dataset-construction paper unrelated to agent-task verification.

title: A Chain-of-Thought Is as Strong as Its Weakest Link: A Benchmark for Verifiers of Reasoning Chains
why: REVEAL introduces step-level verification of CoT reasoning chains (separating relevance, attribution, and logical correctness per step) precisely because full-chain/final-answer correctness can mask invalid intermediate reasoning -- the clearest structural analog in this batch to B1.3's concern that scoped, per-unit checks can diverge from whether the whole trajectory's underlying state is actually valid, even though it operates on reasoning-chain steps rather than agent milestones/prerequisite DAGs.

title: Are Machine Rationales (Not) Useful to Humans? Measuring and Improving Human Utility of Free-text Rationales
why: Studies whether machine-generated free-text rationales are actually useful to human decision-makers and how to improve their human utility; a human-AI rationale-usefulness study unrelated to milestone-verifier bypass.

title: Adaptive and Personalized Exercise Generation for Online Language Learning
why: Combines a knowledge-tracing model with controlled text generation to produce personalized language-learning exercises adapted to a student's estimated knowledge state; an educational NLG application unrelated to agent-task verification.

title: An Inclusive Notion of Text
why: A position paper proposing a systematized, inclusive notion of 'text' as an NLP research object (documenting what information text carries and how it is transformed into NLP artifacts); a conceptual/terminological paper unrelated to checkpoint-bypass verification.

title: Hardening Agent Benchmarks with Adversarial Hacker-Fixer Loops
why: Nearest 2026 neighbor to the motivating claim: directly measures outcome-verifier hackability at scale (323/1,968 tasks, 16%, five terminal-agent benchmarks) and patches verifiers via a hacker-fixer-solver loop. Whole-task outcome verifiers only: no milestone/prerequisite structure, no conditional bypass estimand, no disjoint terminal-state oracle, no locality-vs-weakness attribution. Added 2026-08-15 review pass; verified via arXiv export API (title+date match).

title: SWE-Marathon: Can Agents Autonomously Complete Ultra-Long-Horizon Software Work?
why: Natural-incidence precedent for RQ2: 13.8% of unprompted real-agent rollouts exhibit reward-hacking behavior (detected exploit attempts via adversarial review). Not the conditional verifier-complete-yet-terminally-inconsistent estimand; no prerequisite DAG, no per-milestone locality-scoped checkers, no oracle-error netting. Added 2026-08-15 review pass; verified via arXiv export API.

title: Hack-Verifiable Environments: Towards Evaluating Reward Hacking at Scale
why: Constructed-arm paradigm precedent for RQ1: embeds detectable reward-hacking opportunities into environments so exploitation is verifiable by design (TextArena). Single evaluation signal per environment; no multi-step milestone verification, terminal state-consistency oracle, or locality attribution. Added 2026-08-15 review pass; verified via arXiv export API.

title: SWE-Milestone: Evaluating AI Agents on Continuous Software Evolution
why: Deployed-practice evidence: DeepCommit reconstructs verifiable Milestone DAGs from commit logs and grades agents milestone-by-milestone. Uses milestone verification as instrument, assumes its sufficiency; does not audit it. Added 2026-08-15 review pass; verified via arXiv export API.

title: Adaptive Milestone Reward for GUI Agents
why: Deployed-practice evidence on the training-reward side: ADMIRE anchors RL rewards to dynamically distilled milestones and names process-reward proneness to reward hacking. Reward-design method, not a bypass measurement. Added 2026-08-15 review pass; verified via arXiv export API.

title: The Verification Horizon: No Silver Bullet for Coding Agent Rewards
why: Position/analysis: every coding-agent verifier is a proxy for intent; characterizes verification-signal quality along scalability/faithfulness/robustness. No formal locality model or bypass-rate estimand. Added 2026-08-15 review pass; verified via arXiv export API.
